title: Eccentric Dust Ring in the IRS 48 Transition Disk
question: What is the detailed structure of the dust ring and central cavity in the Oph IRS 48 transition disk, and what are the implications for its inner disk, orbital eccentricity, and proper motion of the crescent-shaped structure?

data.bands: Band 7 (0.87 mm); archival Band 9 (440 um) and Band 7 (870 um)

what.value: Stellar parallax, proper motion (-8.72 mas/yr in RA, -24.4 mas/yr in Dec), and 2016 position of IRS 48

evidence.quote: We use the parallax, the proper motion, and the location of the IRS 48 star from Gaia DR3 (cite: GaiaDR3).

According the Gaia DR3, in the year 2016, the star is at ($16^{\rm h}27^{\rm m}37\mbox{$^{\rm s}\mskip-7.6mu.\,$}180$,$-24^{\circ}30'35\mbox{$''\mskip-7.6mu.\,$}416$). It has an proper motion of $-8.72\rm\, mas/yr$ in RA and $-24.4\rm\, mas/yr$ in Dec.

what.value: Disk inclination angle of 50 deg, position angle of 100 deg, and counter-clockwise rotation direction

evidence.quote: with respect to the counter-clockwise rotation of the disk (cite: Bruderer2014)
Assuming an inclination angle of $50^\circ$ and a position angle of $100^\circ$ (cite: Bruderer2014), we deproject the image to the disk plane.

what.value: Stellar mass (2 M_sun), effective temperature (9520 K), and bolometric luminosity (17.8 L_sun)

evidence.quote: The star IRS 48 was estimated as a $2\rm\, M_\odot$ star using kinematic modeling (cite: Brown2012). The effective temperature and the bolometric luminosity was estimated as $9520$ K and $17.8\rm\, L_\odot$ ((cite: Brown2012); rescaled by (cite: Francis2020) using new distance from Gaia DR2 data (cite: GaiaDR2)).

what.value: 34 GHz flux of the central source (36 uJy)

evidence.quote: Taking the flux of the central source at 34 GHz ($36\rm\, \mu$Jy, (cite: vanderMarel2015)) and the flux derived in our 2D-Gaussian fit at 343.5 GHz ($221\rm\, \mu$Jy), we obtain a spectral index of $0.78\pm0.20$.

what.value: Archival high-resolution ALMA observations from 2012, 2014, 2015, and 2018

evidence.quote: Since (cite: vanderMarel2013), the IRS 48 has been observed with ALMA at high resolution multiple times ((cite: vanderMarel2015; Francis2020; vanderMarel2021_IRS48); 2021 observations in this study).
We adopt a systemic velocity of 4.55 km/s as in (cite: vanderMarel2021_IRS48) and the resulting velocity map is similar to their Fig. 1.

recipe.goal: Self-calibrate and image the Band 7 dust continuum
recipe.method: Combine the four continuum basebands while excluding channels with potential line emission, perform two iterations of phase-only self-calibration on Stokes I, and clean using CASA tclean with the Hogbom algorithm and Briggs weighting
key_parameters: Self-calibration solution intervals: infinite (1st iteration) and 25 seconds (2nd iteration)

recipe.goal: Determine the stellar center at the epoch of observation
recipe.method: Propagate the Gaia DR3 2016 stellar coordinates to the 2021.5 observation epoch using Gaia DR3 proper motions
assumptions: Distance = 136 pc from Gaia DR3 parallax

recipe.goal: Deproject continuum image and fit elliptical ring
recipe.method: Deproject the continuum image to the disk plane and fit an ellipse parameterized by semi-major axis, eccentricity, and major-axis position angle (First with focus fixed at the star, then with free focus location) by minimizing a custom asymmetric loss function
key_parameters: delta_p = 0.02'', asymmetric loss weighting factor 1.5 for dr > 0
assumptions: Inclination angle = 50 deg, position angle = 100 deg
One focus fixed on the central star (in the baseline fit)

recipe.goal: Fit central source and estimate inner disk dust mass
recipe.method: Fit a 2D Gaussian to the central continuum emission, evaluate stellar photosphere and ionized wind contributions, and calculate optically thin thermal dust mass from the 3-sigma contour mean flux density and area
key_parameters: Area within 3-sigma contour = 291 au^2; mean flux density = 8.65e-5 Jy/beam

recipe.goal: Measure multi-epoch proper motion of the crescent peak
recipe.method: Use CASA imfit to fit a 2D Gaussian to the crescent across 5 ALMA epochs spanning 9 years (2012-2021) and perform a linear fit to the peak positions after subtracting the Gaia stellar proper motion
key_parameters: 5 epochs (2012.50, 2014.45, 2015.58, 2018.63, 2021.50); epoch uncertainty = 0.1 yr; astrometric error doubled for resolution < 0.15''
assumptions: Keplerian velocity v_K = 5.438 km/s at r = 60 au; distance = 136 pc; negligible azimuthal offset between Band 9 and Band 7 peaks; Gaia astrometric error ignored

recipe.goal: Model line-of-sight velocity map of the eccentric orbit
recipe.method: Compute the line-of-sight velocity map and iso-velocity contours for the best-fit e = 0.27 elliptical orbit and compare with a circular Keplerian rotation model
assumptions: Gas is co-moving with the dust

score_reason: Calibration, self-calibration intervals, imaging algorithm/weighting, deprojection angles, dust mass assumptions, and the analytic form of the ellipse-fitting loss function are all explicitly stated. Minor gaps remain in the exact line-flagging channel ranges, tclean stopping criteria, and pixel-masking boundaries for the ellipse loss function and imfit.
rediscovery_reason: All four ALMA project codes are public in the archive, the core data processing uses standard CASA tasks (self-calibration, tclean, imfit) with well-specified parameters, and the main scientific findings are concrete numerical values (eccentricity, semi-major axis, central source flux/mass, and multi-epoch proper motion).
